findings.source_passage: you know one really has the devil of a time getting anything out of it! And if we have to fill up a blue form and send it in, and then, after three months, they send us a green one, and so on--well, that won't be much use, will it?
findings.source_locator: Tuppence's speech about government bureaucracy, before Carter laughs outright
findings.why_it_matters: This is a sharply voiced comic aside — Tuppence's ironic dig at government red tape — that establishes her irreverent register and prompts Carter's only open laugh in the scene. Its deletion flattens both her voice and the warm comedic beat that precedes Carter's generosity.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'blue form / green form' riff verbatim or close to it, including the prompt for Carter's laugh, which is the payoff moment.

findings.source_passage: He looks so awfully tired and bored, and yet you feel that underneath he's just like steel, all keen and flashing. Oh! She gave a skip. Pinch me, Tommy, do pinch me. I can't believe it's real!
findings.source_locator: After leaving Carter's house, Tuppence's outburst
findings.why_it_matters: The draft keeps the 'steel, all keen and flashing' line and the pinch request but excises the physical action ('She gave a skip') and the exclamation 'Mr. Beresford obliged. Ow! That's enough!' — a brief but distinctly Christie comic beat that gives the exuberance a bodily reality and Tommy a tiny characterising moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'She gave a skip' and the 'Mr. Beresford obliged. Ow! That's enough!' exchange to preserve the physical comedy.

findings.source_passage: He went into oil, and he went into steel, and he played a bit with railroads, and I can tell you he made Wall Street sit up!
findings.source_locator: Julius's account of his father's fortune, in the middle of his explanation
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is stylistically distinctive — the anaphoric 'he went into…' triplet followed by the colloquial 'made Wall Street sit up' is the voice-establishing beat that makes Julius sound authentically American and larger-than-life. The draft replaces it with the flat summary 'oil, steel, railroads.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the anaphoric structure and 'made Wall Street sit up' verbatim to preserve Julius's characterising voice.

findings.source_passage: See here, he declared. This isn't Sicily! No demanding ransom or threatening to crop her ears if I refuse. These are the British Isles, so quit the funny business, or I'll just sing out for that beautiful big British policeman I see out there in Piccadilly.
findings.source_locator: Julius's suspicious outburst before Tommy explains their role
findings.why_it_matters: This comedic set-piece — 'not Sicily,' 'crop her ears,' 'beautiful big British policeman in Piccadilly' — is Julius's most colourful single speech, a period-register flourish that crystallises his comic-American bluntness. Its complete absence is a mild but real flattening of his introduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the Sicily/ransom image and the Piccadilly policeman line to preserve Julius's comic-blustering register.

findings.source_passage: It's more respectable than I thought it would be, said Tuppence thoughtfully. Luckily I haven't got your craving for crime!
findings.source_locator: Exchange between Tommy and Tuppence after leaving Carter, before the Julius P. Hersheimmer reminder
findings.why_it_matters: This short exchange is a light but characterising beat — Tuppence's mock-wistfulness about respectability and her jab at Tommy's 'craving for crime' — that carries the chapter's running ironic tone about their adventure fantasies.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'more respectable than I thought' exchange and Tommy's reply; it is brief and fits within the budget.

summary: Three medium-severity findings (missing government-red-tape comic speech, missing 'Wall Street sit up' anaphora, flattened physical skip-and-pinch action) and two low-severity voice flattenings collectively erase much of the segment's comic register and character voice; regeneration recommended.
